statement: An intrinsic necessary-and-sufficient arithmetic classification of all characteristic-zero reconstruction fields remains unresolved. The corrected Qsolv Gm test is proved in F.23, all-scheme reconstruction over finite extensions of Qsolv in F.31, and the enlarged sufficient class of all subfields of finitely generated extensions of Qsolv in F.37. F.38-F.41 give finite-extension invariance, intrinsic necessary centralizer conditions and explicit excluded field families, without proving sufficiency. F.42 proves that G_k with its full cyclotomic character, all open-subgroup data and field cardinality cannot determine the property.

manuscript_passages: MPL149, manuscript p.25v, scan52; LM5-F.44 and prompt F2
notes: Literal R27 has no characteristic-zero reconstruction fields by F.1. Corrected F.50 holds in F.7 and is contained in F.37. F.37 proves the all-scheme property over every subfield of a finitely generated extension of Qsolv, using finite detection, arithmetic equivariance, generalized Albanese, the finitely generated-field integral Tate-Hom theorem, Gauss-valuation integrality, and algebraic descent. These sufficient field classes and CHW's exact topos criterion do not classify all fields by intrinsic arithmetic conditions. The new necessary conditions are slimness of G_k and injectivity of Aut(E)->Out(G_E) for every finite E/k, equivalently trivial centralizer of G_E in Aut(kbar). Algebraically closed, real-closed and all characteristic-zero Laurent-series fields are excluded. The converse remains unproved. F.42 gives the explicit countable pair Q and A(Q), with the same Galois/cyclotomic data but different reconstruction behavior. The classification must therefore use additional arithmetic information. F.43 further supplies the virtually-prosolvable-normal-closure sufficient class over finitely generated characteristic-zero subfields; no converse is proved. F.44 now extends the positive sufficient class to proper subgroup/quotient/extension-closed finite-group subclasses and gives its explicit alternating-subquotient formulation; the Q^{C60} example is outside F.43. No intrinsic necessity is proved. F.45 adds every positive-transcendence subfield of a finitely generated Qbar extension, including Qbar(t), which is outside F.44. Algebraic subfields are excluded; no all-field converse is asserted. F.46 gives the equivalent sufficient condition of a virtually pro-C geometric normal-closure group over a positive-transcendence finitely generated model; Qbar(t)^solv is outside both F.44 and F.45. The total arithmetic normal-closure group is not assumed pro-C, and no converse for all fields is claimed. F.47 gives a further intrinsic necessary obstruction: the stated henselian residue-characteristic-zero valuation cannot occur in a finite-transcendence-degree reconstruction field. It also excludes the ordinary algebraic power-series field A0(F) and every algebraic extension, using a full-inertia centralizing substitution. F.48 strengthens F.47 to every finite-rational-rank henselian residue-characteristic-zero valuation satisfying the Abhyankar equality. It supplies a necessary obstruction only and makes no assertion for valuations with transcendence defect. F.49 adds Hilbertian algebraic Galois extensions k/D with D finitely generated of positive transcendence degree and Qbar contained in k, and every finitely generated L/k. Smallness of Gal(k/DQbar) supplies Hilbertianity and descent to positive-transcendence subfields. The alternating-product and universal-tripod examples lie outside the entire F.46 class even after changes of model. This does not supply an intrinsic converse. Hilbertianity is not necessary because the radically closed Qsolv example already reconstructs. For a henselian valuation with transcendence defect, K need not be algebraic over the coefficient-field/independent-parameter henselization, so F.32 cannot transfer the present obstruction.
